set_aside.subject: owner form value conversion failures
set_aside.text:
every other field a page writes or a request is read by is a row of
the imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant, a tuple's position in place of
the imported `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` constant
set_aside.question: When a listed field is present but its text cannot be read as the row's integer, Boolean or enumeration kind, what must `owner_interface` supply to `operations`, and which refusal must result?
options: Preserve a field-specific invalid value so the owning operation refuses it at stage (4).
Treat the field as absent, allowing a required destination to become `missing_value`.
Treat the whole form as unreadable and hand on no values, CSRF value or credential.
Have `owner_interface` return its own transport error without calling `operations`.
set_aside.default_guess: Preserve a field-specific invalid value and let `operations` produce the applicable stage-(4) refusal while retaining the valid CSRF value and other readable fields.

witness.initial: A valid owner session has a rendered correction form whose revision field is listed as an integer in `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`.
events: The browser submits the valid session cookie and CSRF value, but sends `abc` as the revision text.
outcomes: The invalid revision is preserved and the request reaches the ordinary value/version checks, producing a field-specific refusal.
The conversion makes the form unreadable or the revision absent, producing a missing-CSRF, missing-value or stale refusal instead.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different refusal code, stage or page.

set_aside.subject: duplicate occurrences of one owner form field
set_aside.text:
every other field a page writes or a request is read by is a row of
the imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant
set_aside.question: If a request contains the same listed field name more than once, what single value or failure must `owner_interface` pass to `operations`?
options: Reject the ambiguity through the ordinary invalid-request path.
Use the first occurrence.
Use the last occurrence.
Collect every occurrence, but only for destinations explicitly declared as collections.
set_aside.default_guess: Reject duplicate occurrences unless the row explicitly denotes an indexed collection.

witness.initial: A valid session has a form with one listed `project_id` field.
events: The browser submits two `project_id` values under that field name together with a valid CSRF value.
outcomes: The request is refused as ambiguous and no project is changed.
The first or last value is selected and that project is changed.
witness.observer: The owner and the affected project records see the difference.

set_aside.subject: absent Boolean form fields
set_aside.text:
every other field a page writes or a request is read by is a row of
the imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant
set_aside.question: When a Boolean row's field is absent, as an unchecked HTML checkbox normally is, does it fill the destination with `false`, leave it absent, or make the request invalid?
options: Absent means `false`.
Absent remains absent and the owning operation decides whether that is allowed.
Every Boolean control must submit an explicit true-or-false value; absence is invalid.
set_aside.default_guess: Require an explicit value for required Boolean inputs and otherwise preserve absence; rendered forms should emit an explicit false value where unchecked must mean false.

witness.initial: The owner is granting a project and leaves the `make active` control unchecked.
events: The browser omits the unchecked control from the submitted form.
outcomes: The request supplies `false`, grants the project and leaves the active project unchanged.
The request supplies no value and is refused or interpreted by a later module differently.
witness.observer: The owner and the session's access record see whether the grant succeeds.

set_aside.subject: unlisted and action-irrelevant submitted fields
set_aside.text:
every other field a page writes or a request is read by is a row of
the imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant
set_aside.question: Must an unlisted field, or a listed field belonging to another action, be ignored, refused as outside the closed form, or make the whole form unreadable?
options: Ignore every unlisted field and every listed value the selected action does not consume.
Refuse any unlisted field but ignore listed fields irrelevant to the action.
Refuse both unlisted and action-irrelevant fields.
Treat either case as an unreadable form and discard all parsed values.
set_aside.default_guess: Ignore unlisted fields as M29 requires, but refuse a listed field that is not admitted for the selected action so accidental cross-action inputs cannot affect confirmation bindings.

witness.initial: A valid correction form contains all expected fields and a valid CSRF value.
events: The browser adds an unlisted `role=owner` field and a listed field normally used by a different owner action.
outcomes: The extra fields are ignored and the correction proceeds.
The request is refused or all of its values are discarded.
witness.observer: The owner sees success versus refusal, and the project may or may not change.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: functional uniqueness of OWNER_FORM_FIELDS rows
set_aside.text:
The table holds the names
so that the page and the reader cannot name a field differently (Route B
runs of 2026-11-25).
set_aside.question: What uniqueness guarantees must `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` satisfy when two rows share an external name, share a destination path, or overlap through a tuple-position pattern?
options: Every external name or position pattern and every destination path is unique.
Several external names may alias one destination, but one external name may never select several destinations.
Rows may overlap and declaration order chooses the first match.
Rows may overlap only when their owner actions are disjoint.
set_aside.default_guess: Allow no ambiguous external-name or position-pattern match; permit aliases only if State 5 explicitly guarantees that all aliases parse identically into the same destination.

witness.initial: A release contains two rows whose external field pattern matches the same submitted name but whose destinations differ.
events: A page renders the name for the first destination.
The browser submits it and the reader evaluates the table.
outcomes: The reader fills the first destination.
The reader fills the second destination or rejects the release/request.
witness.observer: `operations` sees different owner inputs and may act on a different target or value.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: concrete owner field names, paths and tuple-position encoding
set_aside.text:
The row
gives the field's name, its path in the owner request or its values, with a
tuple's position marked; which of the two it fills; and how its text is
read: as text, as an integer, as true or false, or as an enumeration
member's value.
set_aside.question: Which concrete field-name syntax, destination-path representation and tuple-position substitution must State 6 declare?
options: Bracketed indices such as `picks[0].project_id` with a structural destination path.
Delimited names such as `picks.0.project_id` with a structural destination path.
Repeated field names whose occurrence order supplies tuple positions.
Opaque generated field identifiers mapped to explicit structural paths by the table.
consequences: Bracketed indices are familiar to HTML form tooling but require an exact escaping and sparse-index rule.
Delimited names are simple but require escaping or forbidding delimiter characters in path components.
Repeated names avoid index syntax but make grouping nested tuples and detecting duplicates harder.
Opaque identifiers remove parsing ambiguity but make generated HTML and diagnostics less readable.
set_aside.requirement:
The table holds the names
so that the page and the reader cannot name a field differently (Route B
runs of 2026-11-25).
set_aside.default_guess: Use bracketed numeric indices and explicit structural destination paths, with dense zero-based positions.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: serialized Boolean and enumeration form values
set_aside.text:
how its text is
read: as text, as an integer, as true or false, or as an enumeration
member's value.
set_aside.question: Which exact textual encodings must State 6 choose for Boolean and enumeration values written by pages and read from requests?
options: Canonical `true`/`false` and the exact model enumeration values, case-sensitive.
HTML-style `on` for true with absence for false, and exact enumeration values.
Numeric `1`/`0` and exact enumeration values.
Row-specific serialized tokens declared alongside each field.
consequences: Canonical Boolean text gives a symmetric round trip and clear rejection of other tokens.
HTML checkbox semantics are conventional but make absence part of Boolean decoding.
Numeric tokens are compact but less self-describing and need an explicit rejection rule for other integers.
Row-specific tokens are flexible but enlarge the table and can make equivalent fields inconsistent.
set_aside.requirement:
how its text is
read: as text, as an integer, as true or false, or as an enumeration
member's value.
set_aside.default_guess: Use case-sensitive `true` and `false`, and exact case-sensitive model enumeration values.
